title: Chile: History & Governance Update — May 09, 2026
summary: José Antonio Kast's first months as Chile's most conservative president since Pinochet have been turbulent: his approval crashed from 59% to 29% within weeks of taking office following fuel price hikes of 32–62%, triggering the largest cacerolazos since the 2019 estallido. Student protests erupted in Santiago on April 29 against education budget cuts, while May Day marches saw CUT-led union demands for wage protection. Business confidence fell below the 50-point pessimism threshold in April. On the positive side, lithium exports nearly tripled year-on-year with Q1 revenue hitting $1.108 billion — up 147.7% — as the Codelco–Rio Tinto partnership ramps production at Maricunga and Nuevo Cobre. The IMF's May 4 Article IV mission flagged fuel-driven inflation risks while acknowledging Chile's structural strengths.
